en: When both houses of Congress pass a bill, the President signs it to officially turn the proposed legislation into a binding national law.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator where hot water in outer jars warms the inner chamber to safely keep premature babies alive.
The Katarungang Pambarangay requires neighbors to first settle minor disputes through their local barangay captains before they are allowed to file formal court cases.
Builders installed translucent Capiz shells in wooden window frames to allow sunlight to enter dark rooms while protecting the interior from heavy tropical rain.
Dr. Ramon Barba discovered that spraying potassium nitrate on mango trees tricks the plants into flowering simultaneously, allowing farmers to harvest fruit year-round.
The Supreme Court exercises judicial review to declare a President's executive order unconstitutional, effectively stopping the executive branch from enforcing an illegal rule.
The Ifugao people carved stone-walled terraces into mountains so that rainwater and mountain springs flow downward through a shared canal system to irrigate every rice paddy.
Voters shade ovals on a ballot, and the Precinct Count Optical Scanner reads these marks to instantly tally votes and transmit results to the central server.
Weavers create a banig mat by tightly interlacing dried buri palm leaves in an over-and-under pattern, which locks the fibers together to form a sturdy sleeping surface.
Gregorio Zara invented a two-way videophone by converting sound waves into electrical signals for audio and using a camera to transmit moving visual images over wires.
The ancient Baybayin script writes words using syllable blocks, where a single consonant-vowel character represents a sound, and a small mark modifies the vowel.
The national government automatically shares a portion of its internal revenue taxes with local government units, providing them the funds needed to operate and build local projects.
